BiblicalUsage: Ashbea is named once, as the head of the house of them that wrought fine linen, of the house of Ashbea, in the families of Shelah the son of Judah. The verse gives his house and his trade and nothing more.
TheologicalSignificance: A linen worker named once in a list of Judah's families tells me that God counts the tradesmen as well as the kings, and that fine linen for the house of God was a family calling.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
